reason: Owner directive 2026-11-03 (ADR0023) removes a delegated-work judge and time-based checkpoints as delivery gates while preserving evidence-driven experimentation and independent blind instruction evaluation.

edits.before: - The rigor level, biased high. One-way doors and high blast radius get more. Reversible low-stakes steps get less. Rigor is gates and artifacts, not "try harder".
edits.after: - The implementation and proof depth the risk needs. Rigor changes that depth, not the delivery gates owned by [ship-loop](../ship-loop/SKILL.md).

edits.before: Present the framing and tradeoffs before committing to a long run. Reversible work proceeds (the **never-block-on-the-human** principle skill), but a multi-hour run earns one checkpoint.
edits.after: State the framing and tradeoffs, then proceed with authorized reversible work under the **never-block-on-the-human** principle skill. Use the installed [watchdog](../watchdog/SKILL.md) for open-ended supervision rather than a time-based approval checkpoint.

edits.before: - Pair delegated work with a judge. If a worker games the gate, reset and harden the contract. If the gate itself is wrong, fix the gate in its own change rather than routing around it.
edits.after: - The author proves the unit on the real running path and uses the installed [ship-loop](../ship-loop/SKILL.md) skill for delivery. Independent blind judges belong to instruction evaluation, not merge approval.

edits.before: Check the whole against the Phase A predicate on the real product, not just the harness. Encode any recurring correction as a gate, a lint rule, a check, or a script (the **encode-lessons-in-structure** principle skill).
edits.after: Check the whole against the Phase A predicate on the real running product, not just the harness. Deliver changed artifacts through the installed [ship-loop](../ship-loop/SKILL.md) skill. Encode a recurring correction structurally when the evidence warrants it under **encode-lessons-in-structure**.
